column2: “Look!{r}{p}
There's a fork in the road!”
It was true.
A crossroads was emerging within the circle of light.
It was a road we hadn't noticed on the way here.
“Which way should we go?”
{n2} said in a voice full of anxiety.
“I have a feeling we're really going to get lost here...”
“What...
already with that?”
{n2} glared at me with a look that said, how pathetic.
“No, it's just a feeling.{r}{p}Ah, if only I had
paper and a pen...{r}{p}I really wish I could make a map...”
A thick fir tree grows in the middle of the crossroads.
One of its branches stretches long, as if pointing toward one of the four roads.
For convenience, I decided to call the road that branch points toward north, the one on the right east, and the one on the left west.
And then we...
We went west.
Heading west, the snow got deeper and deeper, and my legs began to sink up to the knees.{g}
this isn't a road, is it?{r}{p}{g}
Looks like we can't go any farther.”{g}
yeah, you're right...{g}
Let's go back.”{g}
Heading west, it was a dead end.
“We've been here before!{r}{p}
Come on, get it together!”
{n2} yelled at me.
sorry.”
We went back right away.
We went north.
Following the north road, it split in two again.
The road straight ahead was a steep climb, and the road going west was a gentle climb.
The wind blowing down from the mountaintop seemed determined to keep us from going any farther.
“Hey, which one do you think?”
{n2}, huddled against me, was shivering uncontrollably.
I decided to turn back for now.
“We'd better go back.”
Saying that, we returned to the fir tree.
North was a steep climb, west a gentle climb, and south a downhill slope.
We went down south.
Downhill or not, this was snow.
Just lifting and setting down my feet was hard, and it was in no way easy.
After a while, a familiar-looking tree came into view.
We went east.
Heading east, the road split into two again.{g}
One continued straight, and the other climbed toward the north.{g}
“Which one, I wonder?”{g}
“Ahh,{g}
I want some hot ramen...”{g}
{n2}'s eyes looked strange.{g}
“{n2}, snap out of it!”{g}
When I yelled at the top of my voice, she looked at me as if waking up.{g}
“Sorry.{r}{p}{g}
I just spaced out for a moment...”{g}
“If we get back to the inn, there'll be something warm.”{g}
“Yeah...”{g}
“Come on, let's push on!”{g}
It was a T-junction where the east-west road and the slope from the north met.
“Ahh, I want ramen...”
{n2}'s eyes looked strange.
I decided to just leave her be...
We climbed north.
We went west.
We took the gentle road west.
Following the gentle road, something like a roof came into view by the roadside.{g}
“What is that...”{g}
“Isn't it a bus shelter?”{g}
“Oh, I see...”{g}
It had been buried in snow.{g}
In this snow, naturally no bus would be running.{g}
I tried brushing off a bit of snow and wandering around it in case I could figure out where we were, but it was useless.{g}
“I guess we have to keep going...”{g}
From here the road curved and headed north.{g}
Even after stopping for a moment, the falling snow clung to my boots.{g}
From the cold and exhaustion, both of us were about to collapse.{g}
We kept going north.
I decided to turn back for now.
It was the spot with the bus shelter.
The road stretched north and east.
We went north.
We went east.
The road was a gentle downhill slope.
The wind from the mountain pushed at my back.
Without the snow, walking would have been easy...
Thinking such things with a foggy head, I kept my feet moving.
Before long we ran into a slope running from north to south.
We went east.
Farther east, tree branches spread far over the road, forming an eerie tunnel.
Maybe because of the branches, the snow and wind felt relatively mild.
Every now and then I heard a clump of snow thud down, and my heart jumped.
The forest tunnel curved sharply north.
We decided to turn back west.
It was the dark forest tunnel formed by overhanging trees.
The road curved north and west...
We went west.
My hands were numb.
Even through my winter boots, the cold of the snow seeped in.
I wanted to go home quickly...
That was all our hearts held.
The wind blowing down from the top of the slope wouldn't even let me lift my face.
My cheeks and ears had gone numb from the cold.
{n2} kept walking without complaint, though her teeth were chattering.
The snow and wind seemed to grow fiercer and fiercer.
We were partway along the slope running north to south.
I decided to go down the slope.
As I went down the slope, I thought.
Taking a walk, just the two of us, {n2} and me.
I once fell asleep alone and lonely dreaming of that...
To think it would turn into something life-or-death like this...
Ah, I want to go back to those days.
We went north.
Coming out of the tunnel, maybe because we'd been in a calm place for a while, the wind and snow felt far fiercer than before.{g}
We naturally huddled close, trying to dodge the wind even a little.{g}
“Look!{r}{p}{g}
A pond!”{g}
Where {n2} pointed, there really was a pond frozen pure white.{g}
It seemed we couldn't go any farther than this.{g}
“Shall we go back...”{g}
“Yeah...”{g}
Both of us slumped our shoulders and went back the way we'd come.{g}
“Isn't this the pond we just saw?! Come on!{r}{p}At this rate we'll freeze to death!”
{n2} said in a trembling voice.
Whipping our exhausted bodies, we retraced the road we'd just come.
We went north.
The surroundings were a pitch-black woods.
The feeble light of the flashlight was almost useless against the blizzard.
As I kept staggering up the slope, it split into a road turning east and a road climbing straight north.
I started to feel we would never get back to “Spur.”
Assailed by the bug of weakness, I...
We went back.
Um, where are we now, again...?
I was getting sleepy.
Right...
A road from the east joined the slope running north to south.
I started to feel we would never get back to “Spur.”
Assailed by the bug of weakness, I...
We climbed north.
We turned east.
We went down south.
Um, where are we now, again...?
It was starting not to matter anymore.
Right...
We took the uphill road north.
Shielding our faces from the slashing wind and snow, we leaned forward and climbed the slope.
With the unreliable light of the flashlight, even our footing was uncertain.
Peering far into the darkness, I suddenly thought I saw something flickering.
A hallucination?
Then {n2} cried out.
“Hey, look!{r}{p}
A light!”
It was no hallucination.
She could see it too.
I took a few more steps to get even slightly closer.
It felt as though the ground beneath my feet suddenly vanished.
“Watch out!”
If {n2} hadn't grabbed my arm in time, I would have fallen off the cliff.
The road ended abruptly right there.
“We can see a light over there, and we can't even get to it...”
{n2} said bitterly, but there was nothing to be done.
Dragging our heavy feet, we went back down the slope.
We had climbed again to the cliff we'd nearly fallen off.
As before, a small light was visible in the distance.
“There's just no way across this cliff.{r}{p}Let's go back.”
Dragging our heavy feet, we went back down the slope.
There was a road leading east and a road going down south.
Walking while pulling my legs out of snow up to the shins with every step was awful torture.
The profuse sweat had frozen, and my body heat was draining away fast.
Quickly, I have to get somewhere warm quickly...
Shivering with cold, I...
We went east.
We went down south.
There was a road leading west and a road going down south.
North and east were valleys, their bottoms too deep to make out.
Thinking that if I fell I'd die, I...
We went west.
We went south.
There was a road leading west and a road climbing north.
South was a dark woods, east seemed to be a valley, but I couldn't tell for the darkness and blizzard.
Thinking I wasn't about to die here, I...
We went west.
We climbed north.
The slope grew even steeper, and the blizzard grew fiercer.
Even {n2}, who had never once complained, seemed to have hit her limit.
“{n1}... please,
let me rest a little.”
{n2} dropped to her knees in the snow and begged, clutching my arm.
“No!
If we rest now, we'll freeze to death!”
Hardening my heart, I pulled {n2} to her feet.
“What if...
what if this isn't the way?”
{n2} said something chilling.
I hesitated.
And after agonizing over it at length...
A steep slope continued from north to south.
We went north after all.
We went back south after all.
We climbed north.
We went down south.
The uphill road curved gently and headed east.
The dark, eerie forest had a completely different feel from daytime, yet it looked familiar.
I tried to ask {n2} whether this was the right road, but she was utterly exhausted and seemed to be half-conscious.
If we didn't get there soon, both of us...
Wait a second...
This isn't necessarily the right road.
Wouldn't it be safer to go back to the car and wait for morning?
Even if the engine won't start, at least it would keep the snow off.
No, I've come this far.
No, it's only now that I can turn back.
Praying, we pressed on.
